translations.literal: But Touring Censor Xie Ruyi bore a grudge against Mo; he then falsely accused Mo's son Lai of accepting ten thousand in gold from Meng, obtained Lai's letter through investigation, and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Touring Censor Xie Ruyi, who bore a grudge against Mo, falsely accused Mo's son Lai of accepting ten thousand in gold from Meng, uncovered Lai's letter through investigation, and presented it as evidence.

sentences.zh: 鏌惶恐，乃再疏請征。

translations.literal: Mo grew fearful and again memorialized requesting an expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Mo, alarmed, memorialized again urging an expedition.

sentences.zh: 於是部趣鏌克期進，鏌偕總兵官朱麒發兵八萬，以都指揮沈希儀、張經等統之，分道並入。

translations.literal: Thereupon the ministry pressed Mo to advance by a set date; Mo together with Regional Commander Zhu Qi mobilized eighty thousand troops, placed under Metropolitan Commanders Shen Xiyi, Zhang Jing, and others, who entered by separate routes simultaneously.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry pressed Mo to advance on schedule; he and Regional Commander Zhu Qi mobilized eighty thousand men under Metropolitan Commanders Shen Xiyi, Zhang Jing, and others, who invaded by separate routes at once.

sentences.zh: 猛聞大兵至，令其下毋交兵，裂帛書冤狀，陳軍門乞憐察。

translations.literal: When Meng heard that the great army had arrived, he ordered his subordinates not to engage, tore silk to write a petition of grievance, and presented it at headquarters begging for compassionate review.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng learned the main army was approaching, he ordered his men not to fight, wrote out a petition of grievance on silk, and sent it to headquarters pleading for a fair hearing.

sentences.zh: 鏌不聽，督兵益急，沈希儀斬猛長子邦彥於工堯隘。

translations.literal: Mo would not listen, pressed the troops ever harder, and Shen Xiyi beheaded Meng's eldest son Bangyan at Gongyao Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Mo refused to listen, pressed the advance all the harder, and Shen Xiyi executed Meng's eldest son Bangyan at Gongyao Pass.

sentences.zh: 猛懼，謀出奔，而歸順州知州岑璋，猛婦翁也，其女失愛，璋欲藉此報猛，乃甘言誘猛走歸順，鴆殺之，斬首以獻。

translations.literal: Meng grew afraid and planned flight; but Guishun Prefecture Magistrate Cen Zhang, Meng's father-in-law, whose daughter had fallen from favor, wished to use this to avenge himself on Meng; with honeyed words he lured Meng to flee to Guishun, poisoned and killed him, and presented his severed head.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Meng planned to flee; but Guishun Magistrate Cen Zhang—Meng's father-in-law, whose daughter had lost Meng's favor—saw his chance for revenge; with fair words he lured Meng to Guishun, poisoned him, beheaded him, and sent the head as tribute.

sentences.zh: 六年，鏌以田州平，告捷京師，乃請改田州為流官，並陳善後七事，詔俱從之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Mo reported victory to the capital with Tianzhou pacified, requested conversion of Tianzhou to regular official administration, and set forth seven measures for subsequent pacification—all were approved by edict.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, with Tianzhou pacified, Mo reported victory to the capital, proposed converting Tianzhou to regular administration, and submitted seven measures for lasting pacification; the throne approved them all.

sentences.zh: 鏌留參議汪必東、僉事申惠、參將張經以兵萬人鎮其地，知府王熊兆署府事。

translations.literal: Mo left Consultant Wang Bidong, Vice Commissioner Shen Hui, and Vice Commander Zhang Jing with ten thousand troops to garrison the region; Prefect Wang Xiongzhao served as acting prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Mo left Consultant Wang Bidong, Vice Commissioner Shen Hui, and Vice Commander Zhang Jing with ten thousand troops to garrison the region, while Prefect Wang Xiongzhao served as acting administrator.

sentences.zh: 會必東、惠皆移疾他駐，惟經、熊兆在府，兵勢分，防守稍懈。

translations.literal: When Bidong and Hui both pleaded illness and relocated elsewhere, only Jing and Xiongzhao remained at the prefectural seat; military strength was divided and defense grew somewhat lax.
translations.idiomatic: When Bidong and Hui both withdrew on grounds of illness, only Jing and Xiongzhao remained at the prefectural seat; with forces divided, the garrison's vigilance slackened.

sentences.zh: 於是逆黨盧蘇、王受等乃為偽印，誑言猛在，且借交阯兵二十萬，以圖興復。

translations.literal: Thereupon the rebel partisans Lu Su and Wang Shou and others forged seals, falsely claimed Meng was alive, and said they had borrowed two hundred thousand troops from Jiaozhi to plot restoration.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leaders Lu Su and Wang Shou and their allies forged seals, spread word that Meng still lived, and claimed two hundred thousand Jiaozhi troops would help them restore his rule.

sentences.zh: 蠻民信之，聚眾薄府城。

translations.literal: The tribal people believed them, gathered a host, and pressed upon the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal populace believed them, rallied in force, and marched on the prefectural city.

sentences.zh: 經出擊，兵少不敵，欲引還，而城中陰為內應，呼噪四出，官軍腹背受攻，力戰不支，突圍渡江走，賊逼其後，爭舟溺死者甚眾。

translations.literal: Jing sallied forth to attack; his troops were too few to prevail and he wished to withdraw, but hidden collaborators within the city raised a clamor on all sides; the government army was attacked front and rear, fought hard but could not hold, broke out and fled across the river, the bandits pressed from behind, and many drowned struggling for boats.
translations.idiomatic: Jing sallied out to attack, but his force was too small to prevail and he tried to withdraw; hidden collaborators inside the city then raised a clamor on every side. Caught between front and rear, the government troops fought hard but could not hold; they broke out, fled across the river with rebels pressing from behind, and many drowned struggling for boats.

sentences.zh: 賊沿江置闌索，伏藥弩，夾岸並起。

translations.literal: The bandits set barriers along the river, planted poisoned crossbows in ambush, and struck from both banks at once.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels strung barriers along the river, laid ambushes with poisoned bolts, and attacked from both banks simultaneously.

sentences.zh: 官軍且戰且行，抵向武，失士卒三四百人。

translations.literal: The government troops fought as they marched, reached Xiangwu, and lost three or four hundred soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting as they retreated, the government troops reached Xiangwu having lost three or four hundred men.

sentences.zh: 賊遂入據府城，燒倉粟以萬計。

translations.literal: The bandits then entered and seized the prefectural city, burning granary grain reckoned in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then seized the prefectural city and burned granary stores numbering in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 御史石金上其事，頗委罪前撫盛應期生事召釁，而給事中鄭自璧因請仍檄湖廣永順、保靖兵並力剿賊。

translations.literal: Censor Shi Jin reported the affair, largely blaming the former grand coordinator Sheng Yingqi for provoking trouble and inviting conflict; Supervising Secretary Zheng Zibi thereupon requested that Yongshun and Baojing troops from Huguang again be ordered to join forces in suppressing the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Shi Jin reported the disaster, laying much of the blame on former Grand Coordinator Sheng Yingqi for provoking the crisis; Supervising Secretary Zheng Zibi then requested that Yongshun and Baojing troops from Huguang be redeployed for a joint suppression.

sentences.zh: 帝以四方兵數萬方歸休，豈可復調，命再計機宜以聞。

translations.literal: The emperor said that tens of thousands of troops from all quarters had just returned to rest—how could they be mobilized again? He ordered further deliberation on strategy and a report.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied that tens of thousands of troops from across the empire had only just been stood down for rest—they could hardly be mobilized again; he ordered fresh deliberation on strategy and a report.

sentences.zh: 時盧蘇等雖據府叛，佯聽撫，遣人迎署府事王熊兆。

translations.literal: At the time, although Lu Su and the others held the prefecture in rebellion, they pretended to accept pacification and sent men to welcome the acting prefect Wang Xiongzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Though Lu Su and his allies held the prefecture in rebellion, they feigned willingness to submit and sent men to welcome Acting Prefect Wang Xiongzhao.

sentences.zh: 而其黨王受等糾眾萬余，攻據思恩城，執知府吳期英、守備指揮門祖蔭等。

translations.literal: But his partisan Wang Shou and others mustered more than ten thousand men, attacked and seized Si'en city, and captured Prefect Wu Qiying, Garrison Commander Men Zuyin, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wang Shou and his faction rallied more than ten thousand men, stormed and seized Si'en city, and took Prefect Wu Qiying, Garrison Commander Men Zuyin, and others prisoner.

sentences.zh: 已而釋期英等，亦投牒上官，願聽招撫。

translations.literal: Before long they released Qiying and the others, and also submitted petitions to their superiors expressing willingness to accept recruitment and pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they released Qiying and the others and petitioned the authorities expressing willingness to submit to pacification.

sentences.zh: 都御史姚鏌以兵未集，姑受之以緩其謀。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Yao Mo, because the troops had not yet assembled, temporarily accepted their submission to slow their plotting.
translations.idiomatic: As troops had not yet been assembled, Censor-in-chief Yao Mo provisionally accepted their submission to buy time and thwart their designs.

sentences.zh: 遣諜者檄東蘭、歸順、鎮安、泗城、向武諸土官，各勒兵自效，且責失事守巡參將等官立功自贖。

translations.literal: He dispatched spies with proclamations to the native officials of Donglan, Guishun, Zhen'an, Sicheng, Xiangwu, and other places, ordering each to muster troops and serve the cause, and also held the pacification, circuit patrol, and vice commander officials who had failed in duty to redeem themselves through merit.
translations.idiomatic: He sent agents with dispatches to the native chiefs of Donglan, Guishun, Zhen'an, Sicheng, Xiangwu, and elsewhere, ordering each to raise troops and prove their loyalty, while demanding that the pacification, patrol, and vice commander officials responsible for the disaster redeem themselves through meritorious service.

sentences.zh: 復疏調湖廣永、保土兵，江西汀、贛畬兵，俱會於南寧，並力進剿。

translations.literal: He again memorialized to mobilize Yong and Bao native troops from Huguang and She troops from Ting and Gan in Jiangxi, all to assemble at Nanning and advance together in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized for Yong and Bao native troops from Huguang and She troops from Ting and Gan in Jiangxi to assemble at Nanning and launch a joint suppression campaign.

sentences.zh: 帝以蠻亂日久，鎮巡官受命大征，未及殄絕，輒奏捷散兵，使余孽復滋，罪不容逭。

translations.literal: The emperor said that because the barbarian disturbance had lasted long, the frontier defense officials, having received orders for a major campaign, before exterminating them completely had reported victory and dispersed troops, allowing remnants to flourish again—their offense could not be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that because the tribal unrest had dragged on, the frontier officials—ordered to mount a major campaign—had reported victory and stood down their troops before the rebels were fully destroyed, allowing remnants to regroup; their offense was inexcusable.

sentences.zh: 姑赦前過，益圖新功。

translations.literal: Their past faults were temporarily pardoned, and they were to strive all the more for new merit.
translations.idiomatic: He granted them a temporary reprieve for past failures and ordered them to earn fresh merit.

sentences.zh: 乃起原任兵部尚書新建伯王守仁總督軍務，同鏌討之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the former Minister of War, Wang Shouren, Marquis of Xinjian, was recalled to take overall command of military affairs and, together with Mo, suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shouren, the former Minister of War and Marquis of Xinjian, was then recalled to assume overall military command and join Mo in suppressing the rebels.

sentences.zh: 時受既入思恩，封府庫，以賊兵守之，而自攻武緣。

translations.literal: At the time Shou had already entered Si'en, sealed the treasury, left bandit troops to guard it, and himself attacked Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shou had by then entered Si'en, sealed the treasury, left rebel troops to hold it, and personally led an attack on Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 守巡官鄒輗等率兵至思恩，思恩千夫長韋貴、徐伍等遣壯士由間道入城為內應，夜引官兵奪門，殺賊二十余人，收府印及庫物，護送期英於賓州，因招撫城中未下者。

translations.literal: Pacification official Zou Yi and others led troops to Si'en; the Si'en thousand-household chiefs Wei Gui and Xu Wu sent braves by secret paths into the city as internal collaborators; at night they guided government troops to seize the gate, killed more than twenty bandits, recovered the prefectural seal and treasury goods, escorted Qiying to Binzhou, and then recruited and pacified those in the city who had not yet submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Pacification Official Zou Yi arrived at Si'en with government troops, thousand-household chiefs Wei Gui and Xu Wu of Si'en sent warriors by hidden routes to serve as insiders; by night they guided the troops through the gates, killed more than twenty rebels, recovered the prefectural seal and treasury stores, escorted Qiying to Binzhou, and then set about winning over those in the city who had not yet submitted.

sentences.zh: 時受攻武緣甚急，參將張經堅壁拒守。

translations.literal: At the time Shou pressed the attack on Wuyuan fiercely; Vice Commander Zhang Jing held fast behind strong walls and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shou pressed his assault on Wuyuan with great urgency; Vice Commander Zhang Jing held the walls and refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 鎮守頭目許用與戰，斬其渠帥一人。

translations.literal: Garrison chieftain Xu Yong joined battle and beheaded one of their ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison chieftain Xu Yong fought them in the field and killed one of their chief leaders.

sentences.zh: 賊見援兵大集，乃遁去。

translations.literal: The bandits, seeing relief troops assembling in great numbers, then fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing government reinforcements massing, the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 鏌以聞。

translations.literal: Mo reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Mo reported these developments to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝以田州、思恩賊鋒雖挫，首惡未擒，仍令守仁亟督兵剿撫。

translations.literal: The emperor said that although the bandit momentum in Tianzhou and Si'en had been blunted, the chief culprits had not been captured, and still ordered Shouren urgently to supervise troops in suppression and pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Though rebel momentum in Tianzhou and Si'en had been checked, the chief culprits remained at large; the emperor therefore ordered Shouren to press on urgently with suppression and pacification.

sentences.zh: 守仁威名素重，及督軍務，調兵數萬人至，諸蠻心懾。

translations.literal: Shouren's prestige had always been great; when he took command of military affairs and mobilized tens of thousands of troops, the hearts of the various tribes were awed.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren's reputation carried great weight; once he assumed command and mustered tens of thousands of troops, the tribal peoples were deeply intimidated.

sentences.zh: 守仁至南寧，道中見受等勢盛，度亦未可卒滅，上疏極陳用兵利害。

translations.literal: When Shouren reached Nanning, on the road he saw that Shou and the others' force was strong, judged that they also could not be swiftly destroyed, and memorialized at length on the advantages and disadvantages of using troops.
translations.idiomatic: En route to Nanning, Shouren saw how powerful Shou and his allies had become and concluded they could not be destroyed quickly; he memorialized at length on the pros and cons of military action.

sentences.zh: 兵部議以守仁所見未確，復陳五事，令守仁詳計其宜，於是守仁又疏云：

translations.literal: The Ministry of War deliberated that Shouren's view was not yet certain, again set forth five points, and ordered Shouren to consider in detail what was appropriate; thereupon Shouren again memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War judged Shouren's assessment insufficiently settled, raised five further points, and instructed him to weigh the options carefully; Shouren then submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣奉命於去年十二月至廣西平南縣，與巡按御史石金及藩臬諸將領等會議。

translations.literal: Your subject, having received orders, in the twelfth month of last year reached Pingnan County in Guangxi and conferred with Touring Censor Shi Jin and the provincial officials and commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Having received my orders, I reached Pingnan County in Guangxi last December and conferred with Touring Censor Shi Jin, the provincial officials, and the field commanders.

sentences.zh: 思、田禍結兩省，已逾二年。

translations.literal: The Si'en and Tianzhou calamity had entangled two provinces for more than two years.
translations.idiomatic: The Si'en and Tianzhou crisis had tormented two provinces for more than two years.

sentences.zh: 今日必欲窮兵盡剿，則有十患。

translations.literal: If today one must exhaust troops in complete suppression, there are ten calamities.
translations.idiomatic: If we insist on pursuing total military extermination, there are ten grave risks.

sentences.zh: 若罷兵行撫，則有十善。

translations.literal: If one halts troops and pursues pacification, there are ten benefits.
translations.idiomatic: If we stand down the army and pursue pacification instead, there are ten clear advantages.

sentences.zh: 臣與諸臣，攄心極論，今日之局，撫之為是。

translations.literal: Your subject and the various officials, speaking from the heart and debating to the utmost, concluded that in today's situation pacification is correct.
translations.idiomatic: After candid and exhaustive deliberation among ourselves, we concluded that pacification is the right course for the present situation.

sentences.zh: 臣抵南寧，遂下令盡撤調集防守之兵。

translations.literal: Your subject reached Nanning and thereupon ordered the complete withdrawal of all mobilized defensive troops.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching Nanning, I ordered the complete withdrawal of all mobilized garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 數日內解歸者數萬，惟湖兵數千，道阻遠，不易即歸，仍使分留南寧，解甲休養，待間而動。

translations.literal: Within several days tens of thousands were discharged and sent home; only several thousand Huguang troops, the road being obstructed and distant, could not easily return at once, and were still made to remain in Nanning in detachments, lay down armor and rest, and await an opportunity to act.
translations.idiomatic: Within days tens of thousands were sent home; only a few thousand Huguang troops, blocked by distance and difficult roads, could not return immediately and were kept at Nanning to stand down and rest until called upon.

sentences.zh: 而盧蘇、王受先遣其頭目黃富等訴告，願得歸境投生，乞宥一死。

translations.literal: Lu Su and Wang Shou first sent their chieftains Huang Fu and others to plead, wishing to return to their territory and surrender to life, begging pardon for death.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su and Wang Shou first sent chieftains including Huang Fu to plead their case, asking to return to their homelands and submit, and begging for their lives.

sentences.zh: 臣等諭以朝廷威德，令賫飛牌，歸巢曉諭，期以速降無死。

translations.literal: Your subject and others instructed them in the court's might and virtue, ordered them to carry urgent placards, return to their lairs and announce and instruct, with the promise that swift surrender would mean no death.
translations.idiomatic: We exhorted them with the court's authority and benevolence, gave them urgent placards to carry home, and promised that prompt surrender would spare their lives.

sentences.zh: 蘇、受等得牌，皆羅拜踴躍，歡聲雷動。

translations.literal: Su, Shou, and the others upon receiving the placards all kowtowed in ranks, leaped for joy, and cheers thundered.
translations.idiomatic: When Su and Shou received the placards, they kowtowed in ranks, leaped for joy, and cheers erupted like thunder.

sentences.zh: 尋率眾至南寧城下，分屯四營。

translations.literal: Soon they led their host to below Nanning city and encamped in four camps.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they brought their followers to Nanning and encamped in four divisions below the walls.

sentences.zh: 蘇、受等囚首自縛，與頭目數百人赴軍門請命。

translations.literal: Su, Shou, and the others bound themselves as prisoners with cords on their necks, and with several hundred chieftains came to the army gate to submit to judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Su and Shou bound themselves as prisoners and came to headquarters with several hundred chieftains to surrender.

sentences.zh: 臣等復諭之曰：「朝廷既赦爾罪，爾等擁眾負固，騷動一方。

translations.literal: Your subject and others again instructed them, saying: "The court has already pardoned your crimes, yet you gathered hosts, held fast, and disturbed a whole region.
translations.idiomatic: We admonished them again: "Though the court has pardoned your crimes, you gathered armies, resisted stubbornly, and threw the region into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 若不示罰，何以雪憤？」

translations.literal: If no penalty is imposed, how can public outrage be appeased?"
translations.idiomatic: If no penalty is imposed, how can public outrage be appeased?"

sentences.zh: 於是下蘇、受於軍門，各杖一百，乃解其縛。

translations.literal: Thereupon Su and Shou were brought down at the army gate, each beaten one hundred strokes with the rod, and then their bonds were released.
translations.idiomatic: Su and Shou were then brought before headquarters, each flogged one hundred strokes, and only then were their bonds cut.

sentences.zh: 又諭之曰：「今日宥爾死者，朝廷好生之德；

translations.literal: Again they were instructed: "Today sparing you from death is the court's virtue of cherishing life;
translations.idiomatic: We told them further: "That you are spared death today reflects the court's reverence for life;

sentences.zh: 必杖爾者，人臣執法之義。」

translations.literal: that you must be flogged reflects a minister's duty to uphold the law."
translations.idiomatic: that you must be flogged reflects a minister's duty to uphold the law."

sentences.zh: 眾皆叩首悅服，願殺賊立功。

translations.literal: The host all kowtowed, accepted with satisfaction, and vowed to kill bandits and establish merit.
translations.idiomatic: They all kowtowed in acceptance and pledged to kill rebels and earn merit.

sentences.zh: 臣隨至其營，撫定其眾七萬余人，復委布政使林富等安插，於二月二十六日悉命歸業。

translations.literal: Your subject then went to their camp, pacified and settled their host of more than seventy thousand, again entrusted Provincial Administration Commissioner Lin Fu and others to resettle them, and on the twenty-sixth day of the second month ordered them all to return to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: I then went to their camps, pacified more than seventy thousand followers, entrusted Provincial Administration Commissioner Lin Fu and others with their resettlement, and on the twenty-sixth day of the second month ordered them all back to their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 是皆皇上至孝達順之德，神武不殺之威，未期月而蠻民率服，不折一矢，不傷一人；

translations.literal: All this was owing to Your Majesty's supreme filial piety and accommodating virtue, divine martial power without killing; in less than a full month the tribal people all submitted, without breaking a single arrow or harming a single person;
translations.idiomatic: All this owed to Your Majesty's supreme virtue and merciful martial authority: in less than a month the tribal peoples submitted—without a single arrow loosed or life lost;

sentences.zh: 而全活數萬生靈，即古舞幹之化，奚以加焉。

translations.literal: Yet tens of thousands of living souls were wholly preserved—this is the transformation of the ancient dance with shields and axes; what could surpass it?
translations.idiomatic: and tens of thousands of lives were spared—a pacification worthy of the legendary age when virtue alone subdued foes; what achievement could surpass it?

sentences.zh: 疏聞，帝嘉之，遣行人賫敕獎賚。

translations.literal: When the memorial was reported, the emperor commended it and dispatched a courier bearing an edict of commendation and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, the emperor expressed his approval and sent a courier with an edict of commendation and rewards.

sentences.zh: 於是守仁復疏言：

translations.literal: Thereupon Shouren again memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Shouren then submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 思、田久構禍，荼毒兩省，已逾二年。

translations.literal: Si'en and Tianzhou long fomented calamity, inflicting poison on two provinces for more than two years.
translations.idiomatic: The Si'en and Tianzhou crisis had festered for more than two years, inflicting misery on two provinces.

sentences.zh: 兵力盡於哨守，民脂竭於轉輸，官吏疲於奔走。

translations.literal: Military strength was exhausted in outpost guard duty, the people's substance drained in transport, officials worn out in running about.
translations.idiomatic: Military strength was exhausted by constant outpost duty, the people's resources drained by supply convoys, and officials worn down by endless errands.

sentences.zh: 地方臲卼，如破壞之舟，漂泊風浪，覆溺在目，不待智者而知之矣。

translations.literal: The region was tottering, like a shattered boat adrift on wind and waves—capsizing and drowning before one's eyes; one need not wait for the wise to know it.
translations.idiomatic: The region teetered on the brink, like a shattered boat tossed on stormy seas—disaster imminent and plain for all to see.

sentences.zh: 必欲窮兵雪憤，以殲一隅，無論不克，縱使克之，患且不測。

translations.literal: If one must exhaust troops to assuage grievances and destroy one corner, not to mention failure—even if successful, the calamity would be unpredictable.
translations.idiomatic: To pursue total war for the sake of vengeance and crush one corner of the region would likely fail; even if it succeeded, the consequences would be unpredictable.

sentences.zh: 況田州外捍交阯，內屏各郡，深山絕谷，瑤、僚盤據。

translations.literal: Moreover Tianzhou externally shields Jiaozhi and internally screens the various prefectures; in deep mountains and remote valleys Yao and Liao are entrenched.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzhou moreover stood as an outer bulwark against Jiaozhi and an inner shield for neighboring prefectures; deep mountains and remote valleys were held by Yao and Liao peoples.

sentences.zh: 使盡誅其人，異日雖欲改土為流，誰為編戶？

translations.literal: If all its people were executed, in days to come even if one wished to convert native to regular administration, who would be registered households?
translations.idiomatic: If its people were slaughtered wholesale, who would remain to be registered as ordinary subjects when the day came to replace native rule with regular administration?

sentences.zh: 非惟自撤其藩籬，而拓土開疆以資鄰敵，非計之得也。

translations.literal: Not only would one remove one's own barrier fence, but expand territory to benefit neighboring enemies—this is not a sound plan.
translations.idiomatic: Such a course would not only dismantle our own defenses but expand territory to strengthen neighboring enemies—a gravely mistaken policy.

sentences.zh: 今岑氏世效邊功，猛獨詿誤觸法，雖未伏誅，聞已病死。

translations.literal: Now the Cen clan for generations performed border merit; Meng alone through entanglement and error violated the law; although he had not yet submitted to execution, it is heard he already died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: The Cen clan had served the frontier with distinction for generations; Meng alone fell into legal violation through misjudgment—and though he had not yet been executed, report had it that he had already died of illness.

sentences.zh: 臣謂治田州非岑氏不可，請降田州府為田州，而官其子，以存岑氏之後。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that governing Tianzhou cannot be done without the Cen clan; he requests reducing Tianzhou Prefecture to Tianzhou, appointing Meng's son to office, to preserve the Cen lineage.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that Tianzhou cannot be governed without the Cen clan; I propose reducing Tianzhou Prefecture to Tianzhou and appointing Meng's son to preserve the Cen line.

sentences.zh: 查猛有二子，長邦佐，自幼出繼為武靖州知州。

translations.literal: Investigating, Meng had two sons: the eldest Bangzuo, from childhood given in adoption to serve as magistrate of Wujing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Meng had two sons: the eldest, Bangzuo, had since childhood been given in adoption and appointed magistrate of Wujing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 武靖當瑤賊之沖，邦佐才足制馭，宜仍舊職。

translations.literal: Wujing faced the brunt of Yao bandits; Bangzuo's talent sufficed to control them; he should retain his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Wujing lay in the path of Yao raiders; Bangzuo had proven capable of controlling them and should remain in his present post.

sentences.zh: 而今所建州，請以猛幼子邦相授吏目，署州事，俟後遞升為知州，以承岑氏之祀。

translations.literal: As for the newly established prefecture, your subject requests appointing Meng's younger son Bangxiang as clerk, to administer prefectural affairs provisionally, awaiting later promotion in succession to magistrate, to carry on the Cen clan's sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: For the restored prefecture, I propose appointing Meng's younger son Bangxiang as clerk to administer affairs provisionally, to be promoted in due course to magistrate and carry on the Cen line.

sentences.zh: 設土巡檢諸司，即以盧蘇、王受等九人為之，以殺其勢。

translations.literal: Establish native assistant magistrate posts and other offices, appointing Lu Su, Wang Shou, and nine others to them, to diminish their power.
translations.idiomatic: Native assistant-magistrate posts should be created and filled by Lu Su, Wang Shou, and seven others—nine in all—to break up their consolidated power.

sentences.zh: 添設田寧府，統以流官知府，以總其權。

translations.literal: Add Tianning Prefecture, governed by a regular official prefect, to oversee their authority.
translations.idiomatic: Tianning Prefecture should be established under a regular prefect to oversee the overall authority.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 惟以守仁所奏岑猛子，與撫按所報異，令再覆。

translations.literal: Only because Shouren's report on Cen Meng's sons differed from what the grand coordinator and touring censor reported, he ordered reinvestigation.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shouren's account of Cen Meng's sons differed from reports by the grand coordinator and touring censor, the court ordered a reinvestigation.

sentences.zh: 於是守仁言：「臣初議立岑氏後，該府土目及耆老俱言岑猛本有四子：長邦佐，妻張氏出；

translations.literal: Shouren said: "Your subject's initial proposal to establish a Cen heir—the native chiefs and elders of that prefecture all said that Cen Meng originally had four sons: the eldest Bangzuo, born to wife Lady Zhang;
translations.idiomatic: Shouren wrote: "When I first proposed establishing a Cen heir, the native chiefs and elders of the prefecture all stated that Cen Meng originally had four sons: the eldest, Bangzuo, born to his wife Lady Zhang;

sentences.zh: 次邦彥，妾林氏出；

translations.literal: the second Bangyan, born to concubine Lady Lin;
translations.idiomatic: the second, Bangyan, born to concubine Lady Lin;

sentences.zh: 次邦輔，外婢所生；

translations.literal: the third Bangfu, born to an outside maidservant;
translations.idiomatic: the third, Bangfu, born to an outside maidservant;

sentences.zh: 次邦相，妾韋氏出。

translations.literal: the fourth Bangxiang, born to concubine Lady Wei.
translations.idiomatic: the fourth, Bangxiang, born to concubine Lady Wei.

sentences.zh: 猛嬖溺林氏而張失愛，故邦佐自幼出繼武靖。

translations.literal: Meng doted on Lady Lin while Lady Zhang lost favor, so Bangzuo from childhood was given in adoption to Wujing.
translations.idiomatic: Meng favored Lady Lin while Lady Zhang fell from favor, so Bangzuo was given in adoption to Wujing from childhood.

sentences.zh: 邦彥既死，邦佐得武靖民心，更代亦難其人。

translations.literal: Bangyan having died, Bangzuo had won the hearts of the people of Wujing; to replace him would be difficult to find another suitable man.
translations.idiomatic: Bangyan having died, Bangzuo had won the loyalty of Wujing's people; no suitable replacement could readily be found.

sentences.zh: 欲立邦輔，土目謂外婢所生，名實不正。

translations.literal: If one wished to establish Bangfu, the native chiefs said that as the son of an outside maidservant, name and substance were not correct.
translations.idiomatic: To install Bangfu, the native chiefs argued, would be improper in both name and substance, as he was born to an outside maidservant.

sentences.zh: 惟邦相系猛正派，質貌厚重，堪繼岑氏。

translations.literal: Only Bangxiang was of Meng's legitimate line; his character and bearing were solid, and he could succeed the Cen clan.
translations.idiomatic: Only Bangxiang was of Meng's legitimate line; solid in character and bearing, he was fit to succeed the Cen clan.

sentences.zh: 故當時直謂猛子存者二人，亦所以正名慎始，杜後日之爭也。」

translations.literal: That is why I stated at the time that only two of Meng's sons survived, which also serves to correct the names, take care at the beginning, and prevent disputes in later days."
translations.idiomatic: That is why I stated at the time that only two of Meng's sons survived, which also serves to correct the names, take care at the beginning, and prevent disputes in later days."

sentences.zh: 疏上，如議行。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, it was carried out as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Upon submission of the memorial, the court acted as proposed.

sentences.zh: 八年，守仁於思、田既議設流官，又議移南丹衛於八寨，改思恩府城於荒田，改設鳳化縣治於三里，添設流官縣於思龍，增築五鎮城堡於五屯。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Shouren, having already deliberated on establishing regular officials for Si'en and Tianzhou, also proposed moving Nandan Guard to Bazhai, relocating the Si'en prefectural city to Huangtian, reestablishing the Fenghua county seat at Sanli, adding a regular county at Silong, and building up fortresses at the five stockades of Wutun.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, having already proposed regular administration for Si'en and Tianzhou, Shouren also proposed moving Nandan Guard to Bazhai, relocating the Si'en prefectural seat to Huangtian, establishing the Fenghua county seat at Sanli, adding a regular county at Silong, and fortifying the five stockades at Wutun.

sentences.zh: 及侍郎林富繼之，又言：「田州界居南寧、泗城，交通雲、貴、交阯，為備非一，不宜改設流官。

translations.literal: When Vice Minister Lin Fu succeeded him, he also said: "Tianzhou's borders lie between Nanning and Sicheng, connecting Yunnan, Guizhou, and Jiaozhi; its defenses are manifold—it is not suitable to convert to regular administration.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Minister Lin Fu succeeded him, he argued: "Tianzhou lies between Nanning and Sicheng, with routes linking Yunnan, Guizhou, and Jiaozhi; its defenses are many and varied—it should not be converted to regular administration.

sentences.zh: 南丹衛設在賓州，既不足以遙制八寨，遷八寨又不得以還護賓州。

translations.literal: Nandan Guard is stationed at Binzhou and is insufficient to control Bazhai from afar; moving to Bazhai likewise cannot from there protect Binzhou in return.
translations.idiomatic: Nandan Guard is stationed at Binzhou and cannot effectively control Bazhai from that distance; relocating it to Bazhai would likewise leave Binzhou inadequately protected.

sentences.zh: 為今日計，獨上林之三里，守仁所議設縣者，可遷南丹衛於此。

translations.literal: For today's plan, only at Sanli in Shanglin—the place where Shouren proposed establishing a county—may Nandan Guard be moved.
translations.idiomatic: For the present, only at Sanli in Shanglin—where Shouren had proposed a new county—should Nandan Guard be relocated.

sentences.zh: 夫設縣則割賓州之地以益思恩，是顧彼而失此也。

translations.literal: To establish a county would carve Binzhou's territory to enlarge Si'en—this looks to that and loses this.
translations.idiomatic: Creating a county would carve territory from Binzhou to benefit Si'en—serving one interest at the expense of another.

sentences.zh: 遷衛則扼八寨之吭以還護賓州，是一舉而兩得也。

translations.literal: To move the guard would choke Bazhai's vital point and in return protect Binzhou—one move securing two gains.
translations.idiomatic: Moving the guard would seize the choke point at Bazhai while protecting Binzhou—a single move achieving both aims.

sentences.zh: 然不宜屬田州，而仍屬南寧為便。」

translations.literal: Yet it should remain under Nanning rather than Tianzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Yet it should remain under Nanning rather than Tianzhou."

sentences.zh: 其議與守仁頗有異同，詔從富言。

translations.literal: His proposal differed in part from Shouren's; an edict followed Fu's view.
translations.idiomatic: His proposal partly diverged from Shouren's; the court followed Fu's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 初，邦相兄邦彥有子芝，依大母林氏、瓦氏居，官給養田。

translations.literal: Initially, Bangxiang's elder brother Bangyan had a son Zhi, who lived dependent on his grandmothers Lady Lin and Lady Wa; the government granted sustaining fields.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, Bangxiang's elder brother Bangyan had a son, Zhi, who lived under the care of his grandmothers Lady Lin and Lady Wa; the government granted sustaining estate fields.

sentences.zh: 其後邦相惡蘇專擅，密與頭目盧玉等謀誅蘇及芝。

translations.literal: Afterward Bangxiang resented Su's monopoly of power and secretly plotted with chieftain Lu Yu and others to kill Su and Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Later Bangxiang resented Su's autocratic rule and secretly conspired with chieftain Lu Yu and others to kill Su and Zhi.

sentences.zh: 蘇知之，會邦相又侵削二氏原食莊田，二氏遂與蘇合謀，以芝奔梧州，赴軍門告襲，蘇又為芝疏請。

translations.literal: Su learned of it; as Bangxiang also encroached on the two clans' original sustaining estate fields, the two clans then joined Su in conspiracy; Zhi fled to Wuzhou, came to headquarters to report the attempted murder, and Su also memorialized on Zhi's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Su learned of the plot; when Bangxiang also encroached on the Lin and Wa clans' sustaining estates, the two clans joined Su in conspiracy; Zhi fled to Wuzhou and petitioned headquarters reporting the plot, and Su also memorialized on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 尋令人刺邦相，邦相覺，殺行刺者。

translations.literal: Soon he sent men to assassinate Bangxiang; Bangxiang discovered it and killed the assassins.
translations.idiomatic: Su soon sent assassins against Bangxiang; Bangxiang discovered the plot and killed the assailants.

sentences.zh: 而蘇遂伏兵殺盧玉等，以兵圍邦相宅，誘邦相出，乘夜與瓦氏縊殺之。

translations.literal: Su then set an ambush and killed Lu Yu and others, surrounded Bangxiang's residence with troops, lured Bangxiang out, and in the night together with Lady Wa strangled him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Su then laid an ambush and killed Lu Yu and others, surrounded Bangxiang's residence, lured him out, and in the night strangled him together with Lady Wa.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史曾守約以聞，帝命守臣亟為勘處。

translations.literal: Touring Censor Zeng Shouyue reported it; the emperor ordered frontier officials urgently to investigate and settle the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Touring Censor Zeng Shouyue reported the affair; the emperor ordered local officials to investigate and resolve it at once.

sentences.zh: 蘇之殺邦相也，歸順、鎮安、泗城、向武諸土官群起構難，互相訐奏。

translations.literal: When Su killed Bangxiang, native officials of Guishun, Zhen'an, Sicheng, Xiangwu, and elsewhere all rose to create trouble and mutually impeached one another.
translations.idiomatic: After Su killed Bangxiang, native chiefs of Guishun, Zhen'an, Sicheng, Xiangwu, and elsewhere all stirred up trouble and lodged mutual accusations.

sentences.zh: 當事者謂以岑芝承襲未定，田州無主，致令鄰封覬覦，當給劄付令芝管事。

translations.literal: Those in charge said that because Cen Zhi's succession was unsettled and Tianzhou had no master, neighboring territories were covetous; they should issue a writ entrusting Zhi to administer affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Officials held that because Cen Zhi's succession remained unsettled and Tianzhou lacked a ruler, neighboring territories grew covetous; a writ should be issued entrusting Zhi with administration.

sentences.zh: 蘇又請早給芝冠帶，以撫田州，而自悔罪，願裹糧立功，及追補累年所逋糧賦。

translations.literal: Su also requested early granting of Zhi's formal cap and belt to pacify Tianzhou, while he himself repented, vowed to carry provisions and establish merit, and make up years of delinquent grain levies and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Su also asked that Zhi be invested with official rank without delay to stabilize Tianzhou, while he himself repented, offered to serve at his own expense, and pay years of delinquent grain levies and taxes.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史諸演疏聞，部議以土蠻自相仇殺，當從末減，皆令立功，方準贖罪復官。

translations.literal: Touring Censor Zhu Yan's memorial was reported; the ministry deliberated that since native tribes had mutually killed one another, leniency from the lighter end should apply; all were ordered to establish merit before being permitted to redeem their crimes and restore office.
translations.idiomatic: When Touring Censor Zhu Yan's memorial reached the ministry, it ruled that because the native chiefs had killed one another, the lighter penalty should apply; all were required to earn merit before their crimes could be redeemed and their offices restored.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，芝死，子大壽方四歲。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, Zhi died; his son Dashou was only four years old.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year, Zhi died; his son Dashou was only four years old.

sentences.zh: 土人莫葦冒岑姓，及土官岑施，相煽構亂，提督郎槚奏令思恩守備張啟元暫駐田州鎮之，報可。

translations.literal: The native Mowei falsely assumed the Cen surname, and native official Cen Shi incited each other to create disorder; Grand Coordinator Lang Jie memorialized to have Si'en Garrison Commander Zhang Qiyuan temporarily stationed at Tianzhou to suppress it—the request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: A local man named Mowei falsely claimed the Cen surname, and native official Cen Shi joined him in fomenting unrest; Grand Coordinator Lang Jie memorialized to station Si'en Garrison Commander Zhang Qiyuan at Tianzhou to restore order—the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，田州土官婦瓦氏以狼兵應調至蘇州剿倭，隸於總兵俞大猷麾下。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, Tianzhou native official Lady Wa led Lang troops when mobilized to Suzhou to suppress Japanese pirates, under Regional Commander Yu Dayou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year, Lady Wa of Tianzhou led Lang troops when called up to Suzhou to fight Japanese pirates, serving under Regional Commander Yu Dayou.

sentences.zh: 以殺賊多，詔賞瓦氏及其孫男岑大壽、大祿銀幣，余令軍門獎賞。

translations.literal: Because many bandits were killed, an edict rewarded Lady Wa and her grandsons Cen Dashou and Dalu with silver and silks; the rest were ordered rewarded at headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: For their many kills in battle, the court rewarded Lady Wa and her grandsons Cen Dashou and Dalu with silver and silks; the remainder were to be rewarded at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 四十二年以平廣西瑤、僮功，準岑大祿實受知州職。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, for merit in pacifying Guangxi Yao and Zhuang, Cen Dalu was permitted actually to receive the magistracy.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year, for service in pacifying the Yao and Zhuang of Guangxi, Cen Dalu was formally invested as magistrate.

sentences.zh: 泰昌元年，總督許弘綱奏：「田州土官岑懋仁肆惡起釁，窺占上林，納叛人黃德隆等，糾眾破城，擅殺土官黃德勛，擄其妻女印信，乞正其罪。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Taichang, Governor-General Xu Honggang memorialized, “The Tianzhou native official Cen Maoren has indulged evil and stirred up trouble, looked to occupy Shanglin, accepted the rebels Huang Delong and others, gathered a crowd and broke the city, arbitrarily killed the native official Huang Dexun, and carried off his wife, daughters, seal, and credentials; I beg that his crimes be rectified.”
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taichang, Governor-General Xu Honggang memorialized, “The Tianzhou native official Cen Maoren has indulged evil and stirred up trouble, looked to occupy Shanglin, accepted the rebels Huang Delong and others, gathered a crowd and broke the city, arbitrarily killed the native official Huang Dexun, and carried off his wife, daughters, seal, and credentials; I beg that his crimes be rectified.”

sentences.zh: 詔令岑懋仁速獻印，執送諸犯，聽按臣分別正法，違則進剿。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Cen Maoren quickly to surrender the seal and arrest and deliver the offenders, allowing the inspecting official to punish them separately according to law; if he disobeyed, an exterminating campaign would advance.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Cen Maoren quickly to surrender the seal and arrest and deliver the offenders, allowing the inspecting official to punish them separately according to law; if he disobeyed, an exterminating campaign would advance.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年，巡撫何士晉請免懋仁逮問，各率土兵援剿，有功優敘，從之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi, Grand Coordinator He Shijin requested that Maoren be exempted from arrest and questioning, and that each leader command native troops to assist in suppression, with meritorious service generously rewarded; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianqi, Grand Coordinator He Shijin requested that Maoren be exempted from arrest and questioning, and that each leader command native troops to assist in suppression, with meritorious service generously rewarded; this was approved.

sentences.zh: 田州世岑氏，改流者再，而終不果。

translations.literal: Tianzhou for generations was the Cen clan; conversion to regular administration was attempted twice but ultimately never succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzhou had been held by the Cen clan for generations; conversion to regular administration was attempted twice but never succeeded.

sentences.zh: 盧蘇再叛弒主，終逸於罰，論者以為失刑雲。

translations.literal: Lu Su rebelled again and murdered his lord, ultimately escaping punishment; commentators held it a failure of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su rebelled again and murdered his lord yet ultimately escaped punishment; commentators regarded this as a failure of justice.

sentences.zh: 上林在田州東，宋置，隸橫山寨。

translations.literal: Shanglin lay east of Tianzhou; established in Song, subordinate to Hengshan Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Shanglin lay east of Tianzhou; it was established in the Song and placed under Hengshan Stockade.

sentences.zh: 元屬田州路。

translations.literal: Under Yuan it belonged to Tianzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan it belonged to Tianzhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 洪武二年，土官黃嵩歸附，授世襲知縣，流官典史佐之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongwu, native official Huang Song submitted; he was granted hereditary magistrate, with a regular official recorder to assist.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Hongwu, native official Huang Song submitted; he was granted a hereditary magistracy, assisted by a regular official recorder.

sentences.zh: 恩城州，唐置，宋、元仍舊。

translations.literal: Encheng Prefecture, established in Tang; Song and Yuan kept it unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Encheng Prefecture was established in the Tang; the Song and Yuan dynasties left it unchanged.

sentences.zh: 明初因之，隸廣西布政司，朝貢如例。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Ming it was kept as before, subordinate to the Guangxi Provincial Administration Commission, with tribute audiences as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Ming it remained as before, subordinate to the Guangxi Provincial Administration Commission, with tribute rendered according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 成化十九年，知州岑欽，田州土官岑溥叔也，相仇殺。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Chenghua, Magistrate Cen Qin, uncle of Tianzhou native official Cen Pu, mutually feuded and killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Chenghua, Magistrate Cen Qin—the uncle of Tianzhou native official Cen Pu—fell into mutual feud and bloodshed.

sentences.zh: 溥敗，欽入田州，焚府治，大肆殺掠。

translations.literal: Pu was defeated; Qin entered Tianzhou, burned the prefectural seat, and greatly slaughtered and plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was defeated; Qin entered Tianzhou, burned the prefectural seat, and carried out widespread slaughter and plunder.

sentences.zh: 溥訴於制府，下三司官鞫理。

translations.literal: Pu complained to the supreme commissioner; the three provincial offices' officials were ordered to try the case.
translations.idiomatic: Pu appealed to the supreme commissioner; officials of the three provincial offices were ordered to adjudicate the case.

sentences.zh: 弘治三年，欽復入田州，與泗城土官岑應分據其地。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongzhi, Qin again entered Tianzhou and, with Sicheng native official Cen Ying, divided and occupied its territory.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Hongzhi, Qin again entered Tianzhou and, with Sicheng native official Cen Ying, divided and seized its territory.

sentences.zh: 巡撫秦纮請調兵剿之。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Qin Hong requested mobilizing troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Qin Hong requested that troops be mobilized to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 兵部言兵不可輕動，惟令守臣諭令應縛欽自贖。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War said troops must not be lightly mobilized; they ordered only that the defending officials instruct Ying to bind Qin and redeem himself through service.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War argued that troops must not be lightly mobilized and ordered only that the defending officials instruct Ying to seize Qin and allow him to redeem himself through meritorious service.

sentences.zh: 五年，欽走岑應所借兵，總鎮檄應捕之，欽遂殺應父子。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Qin fled to Cen Ying's place to borrow troops; the supreme commander ordered Ying to capture him, and Qin then killed Ying and his son.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Qin fled to Cen Ying's territory to borrow troops; the supreme commander ordered Ying to capture him, and Qin then killed Ying and his son.

sentences.zh: 已而應弟接佯以兵送欽，亦殺欽父子。

translations.literal: Afterward Ying's younger brother Jie feigned escorting Qin with troops and also killed Qin and his son.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Ying's younger brother Jie feigned escorting Qin with troops and likewise killed Qin and his son in revenge.

sentences.zh: 有司以恩城宜裁革，從之，州遂廢。

translations.literal: The responsible officials held that Encheng should be abolished; the request was granted, and the prefecture was then abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials recommended that Encheng be abolished; the court agreed, and the prefecture was abolished.

sentences.zh: 上隆州，宋置，隸橫山寨。

translations.literal: Shanglong Prefecture was established in the Song and belonged to Hengshan Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Shanglong Prefecture was established in the Song and belonged to Hengshan Stockade.

sentences.zh: 元屬田州路，明因之。

translations.literal: In the Yuan it belonged to Tianzhou Circuit, and the Ming followed this.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuan it belonged to Tianzhou Circuit, and the Ming followed this.

sentences.zh: 後改隸布政司。

translations.literal: Later its subordination was changed to the Provincial Administration Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Later its subordination was changed to the Provincial Administration Commission.

sentences.zh: 洪武十九年，上隆知州岑永通遣從子岑安來貢，賜綺帛鈔錠。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Hongwu, Cen Yongtong, prefectural magistrate of Shanglong, sent his brother’s son Cen An to offer tribute, and patterned silk, plain silk, and paper-money ingots were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Hongwu, Cen Yongtong, prefectural magistrate of Shanglong, sent his brother’s son Cen An to offer tribute, and patterned silk, plain silk, and paper-money ingots were granted.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年，土官知州岑瓊母陳氏來朝，貢馬，賜鈔幣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongxi, Lady Chen, mother of the native official prefectural magistrate Cen Qiong, came to court and offered tribute horses, and paper money and other valuables were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongxi, Lady Chen, mother of the native official prefectural magistrate Cen Qiong, came to court and offered tribute horses, and paper money and other valuables were granted.

sentences.zh: 宣德四年以陳氏為知州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xuande, Lady Chen was made prefectural magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xuande, Lady Chen was made prefectural magistrate.

sentences.zh: 時瓊已卒，無子，土人訴於朝，願得陳氏襲職，故有是命。

translations.literal: At the time Qiong had already died and had no son; the local people appealed to the court, asking that Lady Chen be allowed to succeed to the office, and therefore this order was issued.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Qiong had already died and had no son; the local people appealed to the court, asking that Lady Chen be allowed to succeed to the office, and therefore this order was issued.

sentences.zh: 都康州，宋置，隸橫山寨。

translations.literal: Dukang Prefecture was established in Song and subordinate to Hengshan Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Dukang Prefecture was established under the Song and subordinate to Hengshan Stockade.

sentences.zh: 元屬田州路。

translations.literal: Under Yuan it belonged to Tianzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan it belonged to Tianzhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 洪武間，為蠻僚所據。

translations.literal: During Hongwu it was seized by Man and Liao.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongwu reign it was seized by tribal peoples.

sentences.zh: 三十二年復置，隸布政司。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year it was re-established and subordinated to the provincial administration commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year it was re-established and placed under the provincial administration commission.

sentences.zh: 土官馮姓。

translations.literal: The tribal official was of the Feng surname.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal official was of the Feng clan.

sentences.zh: 其界東南抵龍英，西至鎮安，北至向武。

translations.literal: Its borders reached Longying on the southeast, Zhen'an on the west, and Xiangwu on the north.
translations.idiomatic: Its borders reached Longying to the southeast, Zhen'an to the west, and Xiangwu to the north.
